column3: The Hebrew ends with “because he tore down his altar”; BSB incorporates this into “with the one who has torn down his altar.”
The Hebrew actively says “he called him” without naming the caller or Gideon; BSB names Gideon and uses the passive “was called.”
The Hebrew says they crossed over without explicitly naming the Jordan; BSB supplies “the Jordan.”
The Hebrew says the Spirit “clothed” Gideon and uses a passive summoning verb for Abiezer; BSB has “came upon” and makes Gideon the one who “rallied” the Abiezrites.
The Hebrew repeats the sending of messengers twice and says Manasseh too was summoned; BSB states the sending once and combines the recipients.
The Hebrew leaves Gideon unnamed and explicitly repeats “the fleece”; BSB names Gideon and leaves the second fleece reference implicit.
The Hebrew explicitly names the fleece twice and “all the earth”; BSB uses “it” for the second fleece reference and says “the ground.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “all the earth”; BSB says “the ground.”
